paper_diagnosis: Rare presentation of Toxoplasma pneumonitis in an AIDS patient with disseminated toxoplasmosis diagnosed by next-generation sequencing and PCR
disease_label_per_paper: Toxoplasma pneumonitis and disseminated toxoplasmosis with MRI brain lesions in AIDS
presentation_summary: 39-year-old man from the Democratic Republic of the Congo presented 12 days after immigration to the USA with 5 days of fever, nausea, vomiting, productive cough, nonspecific abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue.
He was ill appearing and cachectic with tachypnea, but cardiac, neurologic, skin, and lymphatic examinations were described as unremarkable.
Chest x-ray showed multinodular changes; CT chest showed bilateral miliary lesions, nodules with developing central cavitation, and bilateral basal consolidation.
He disclosed known untreated HIV infection after admission; CD4 count was 6 cells/uL and HIV-1 viral load was 332,909 copies/mL.
Respiratory status worsened and he required intubation; later MRI brain showed multiple ring-enhancing lesions despite absence of neurologic symptoms.
Toxoplasma was confirmed by plasma microbial cfDNA NGS and positive serum/BAL PCR; he improved after pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, leucovorin, and later ART.

quality_warnings: Toxoplasma NGS, PCR, and serology are stored under microbiology/confirmatory_findings with use_in_ranking:false.
No numeric temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, or full metabolic panel values were provided in the article text used here.
MRI ring-enhancing lesions are included as ordinary anatomic imaging evidence, not as organism-confirming evidence.
